primary.title: The Gospels
primary.author: Matthew, Mark, Luke, John
primary.rationale: The Gospels are the primary accounts of Jesus' life and teachings, considered by many to be divinely inspired and historically significant.

secondary.title: Jesus: A Revolutionary Biography
secondary.author: John Dominic Crossan
secondary.rationale: Crossan offers a scholarly reconstruction of Jesus' life, drawing on historical, archaeological, and textual evidence to present a portrait of Jesus as a peasant sage.

secondary.title: The Historical Jesus: The Life of a Mediterranean Jewish Peasant
secondary.author: John P. Meier
secondary.rationale: Meier's multi-volume work is a comprehensive and detailed scholarly investigation into the historical Jesus, critically examining all available evidence.

secondary.title: Jesus and the Victory of Judaism
secondary.author: Richard A. Horsley
secondary.rationale: Horsley situates Jesus within the context of first-century Judaism, arguing that his teachings and actions were deeply rooted in Jewish social and religious movements.

suggestions.notes: Direct primary sources authored by Jesus himself are not extant. The Gospels are the closest available primary accounts, though their authorship and precise historical accuracy are subjects of scholarly debate. Secondary sources focus on scholarly reconstructions of the historical Jesus.
